    Power curve using Gaussian/Binomial DGPs

    power_curve_mean_dgp.Rd

    Generates a synthetic superpopulation via simulate_crossfit_data() and computes Monte Carlo power curves for the PP mean estimator over a grid of labeled sample sizes using simulate_power_ppi_mean().

    power_curve_mean_dgp(
  n_grid = seq(50, 200, by = 25),
  N,
  theta0 = 0,
  var_f = 0.45,
  var_res = 0.8,
  delta = 0.2,
  family = stats::gaussian(),
  R = 1000,
  alpha = 0.05,
  seed = 1
)

    Arguments

    n_grid

    Integer vector of candidate labeled sample sizes.

    N

    Unlabeled sample size.

    theta0

    Null value for the mean estimand.

    var_f

    Variance of \(f(X)\).

    var_res

    Variance of residuals \(Y - f(X)\).

    delta

    Effect size \(\theta - \theta_0\).

    family

    GLM family passed to the DGP; defaults to stats::gaussian() (with identity link) or stats::binomial() (logistic).

    R

    Number of Monte Carlo replicates passed to simulate_power_ppi_mean().

    alpha

    Two-sided significance level.

    seed

    Random seed forwarded to simulate_crossfit_data().

    Value

    Data frame with the columns produced by power_curve_mean() plus family, theta, and theta0 for downstream plotting.

    Examples

    power_curve_mean_dgp(
  n_grid = seq(50, 200, by = 25),
  N = 3000,
  theta0 = 0,
  var_f = 0.45,
  var_res = 0.80,
  delta = 0.2,
  R = 1000
)
#>     n analytical empirical     abs_diff
#> 1  50  0.3498847     0.373 0.0231153218
#> 2  75  0.4853155     0.510 0.0246845069
#> 3 100  0.6008198     0.582 0.0188198063
#> 4 125  0.6954147     0.696 0.0005853261
#> 5 150  0.7706339     0.754 0.0166338854
#> 6 175  0.8291243     0.836 0.0068757262
#> 7 200  0.8738207     0.871 0.0028206571
